Published Theorem 2.2 on page 1974 gives a Frobenius online-SGD rate and Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 gives fixed-form asymptotic normality for scalar rewards from independent Gaussian matrix contexts.
Published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 bound nearest-neighbor error for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean under an adaptive pooled sequential policy.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD matrix-row upper bound under independent Bernoulli assignments and low-rank arm means.  Its displayed rate has its own fourth-power logarithmic factor and shares only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\) with \(b^0_{nm}\); it does not supply the additional \(\sqrt{\log n}\) maximum-row or \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\) effect-subspace conversion in \(b_{nm}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine whether the observed-data minimax expected normalized maximum-row risk contracts at \(b_{n_\ell m_\ell}\), at an intermediate rate, or not at all; only then determine the normalized constant and an attaining estimator.
open_obligations.obstruction: The constant-propensity packing yields only a \(c b_{nm}\) lower bound.  The new hybrid yields only \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\), which is constant in the nonempty fixed-complexity regime, and the endogenous-target construction lower-bounds only recorded IPW--SVD rather than all observed-data estimators.
open_obligations.attempted: A row-local constant-propensity Fano packing, matrix-Freedman spectral control, deterministic subspace perturbation, the endogenous-target test, and an explicit deterministic-sine fallback were all completed.  They close the two-sided bracket but do not locate the estimator-independent rate inside it.

prose_updates.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make the IPW errors a bounded row-major martingale-difference array.  The strongest uniform same-risk statement on the frozen predictable class is now \(c b_{nm}\le\inf_{\widetilde U}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\), where \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) is an explicit hybrid of recorded IPW--SVD and a deterministic discrete-sine frame.  Recorded IPW--SVD separately retains its \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) expected-risk guarantee and its estimator-specific obstruction.  Nonemptiness of the bounded-outcome class forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); with fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio this gives \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) but \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\), so the available uniform stochastic resolutions do not shrink.  The minimax rate between the lower scale and a constant remains open.  Blind row scaling is certified only at \(d_{nm}\), the rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains a HeartSteps II stress design, and simultaneous dense-query radii retain their separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise results do not settle causal effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment.  On the present bounded-outcome class a constant-propensity packing yields the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\), while the strongest explicit uniform upper bound is constant after hybridizing the loose IPW--SVD radius with a deterministic incoherent frame.  The accepted endogenous-target example prevents claiming \(b_{nm}\)-optimality for recorded IPW--SVD but gives no estimator-independent constant lower bound.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit same-loss minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, with one measurable hybrid estimator on the upper side, together with an estimator-specific IPW obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost remains separate.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the constant-propensity \(c b_{nm}\) converse, the separate \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) expected-risk bound for recorded IPW--SVD, and the hybrid \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) upper bound.  It proves that bounded outcomes force \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\), exposing \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and nonshrinking \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) in the fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime.  It retains the unconditional blind \(d_{nm}\)-resolution inequalities, the explicit Markov witness, and direct finite-sample bands with separate family-size inflation.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and no estimated treatment nuisance.  Its expected-risk guarantee follows from matrix-martingale concentration and deterministic singular-subspace perturbation.  The hybrid compares the deterministic radius \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) with one and otherwise reports the first \(r\) columns of the \(n\)-dimensional discrete-sine orthogonal matrix; it therefore remains measurable from the observed experiment.  The blind procedure replaces entrywise propensities by a clipped empirical row fraction and is controlled only at the explicit \(d_{nm}\) resolution.  Under fixed complexity, bounded aspect ratio, and nonemptiness, both \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\), so neither is a shrinking uniform stochastic radius.  Simultaneous bands use direct recorded-IPW contrasts and deterministic variance envelopes, not feasible multiplier exactness.

prose_updates.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis are the closest rowwise estimator comparator.  Their public Algorithm 1, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3 analyze separate empirical-row-scaled SVD fits for two low-rank arm means under independent Bernoulli assignment and bound matrix-row error.  The only shared rate feature is the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\): their theorem carries its own fourth-power logarithmic factor and armwise assumptions, whereas \(b_{nm}\) additionally contains the maximum-row factor \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the subspace conversion \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\).  No equality or transfer between the two rates is claimed.  For arbitrary arm matrices \(A_1,A_0\), the only algebraic comparison used is \(\operatorname{rank}(A_1-A_0)\le\operatorname{rank}(A_1)+\operatorname{rank}(A_0)\).  Its converse fails even with bounded entries: on a square array, a sufficiently small multiple of the identity is a bounded full-rank common component, and adding a sufficiently small rank-one effect leaves both arms full rank while their difference has rank one.  Thus effect-only low rank does not establish armwise low rank, full-class containment, or rate transfer.

Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen prove two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds for an independently sampled low-rank matrix with independent noise; those results inform the deterministic perturbation and local-packing architecture but not the predictable causal class.  Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah bound unit-by-time counterfactual-mean error under an exogenous factor model.  Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi; Sun, Zhu, and Dubin; Bai and Ng; Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen; Choi and Yuan; Mao, Wong, and Chen; and Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan study other outcome-completion targets, losses, or missingness structures.  These works are informative comparators, not sources of a minimax-rate transfer to the present effect-only class.

Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the recorded-propensity martingale-score reduction, and Tropp supplies the bounded-increment matrix Freedman inequality.  Khan and Ugander analyze scalar affine normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are new objects here and do not refute that method.  Belloni and Oliveira and Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu motivate high-dimensional martingale or multiplier inference, but the retained simultaneous theorem uses finite-sample Freedman radii and a union bound.  Its \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor is a query-family entropy cost, not part of either subspace scale.  Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and omission sensitivity operationally relevant for the HeartSteps II consumer.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Matrix Freedman followed by a deterministic subspace inequality yields \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) for recorded IPW--SVD.  The frozen class permits future singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes, so a leave-one-row argument cannot simply treat those factors as predictable; the explicit obstruction shows this matters for that estimator.  The discrete-sine fallback limits uniform risk to a constant but does not create a shrinking estimator.  Moreover, nonemptiness forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); at fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio, this makes both \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and the blind resolution \(d_{nm}\) at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\).  Hence the remaining gap is between an information lower scale \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and a constant upper bound.  No estimator-independent constant converse, shrinking uniform upper estimator, residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is proved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded IPW conditional mean.  The proved headline is the expected-risk bracket between \(c b_{nm}\) and \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\), with the upper endpoint attained by one explicit observed-data hybrid.  Recorded IPW--SVD separately satisfies the looser \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) bound.  Its endogenous-target witness refutes only uniform \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by that estimator; it does not show that every estimator measurable from \(A,Y,p\) has constant risk.  In the nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, the available IPW and blind stochastic resolutions are nonshrinking, so minimax contraction and the sharp constant remain open.  The blind procedure is certified only up to \(d_{nm}\); the \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is its boundary example and a HeartSteps II stress design, not a refutation of a published normalization method.  Simultaneous inference uses conservative finite-sample direct-IPW radii with a separate query-family entropy factor.

statement_notes.justification: The constant-propensity Fano construction supplies the information-theoretic lower endpoint in the common expected normalized maximum-row risk.
statement_notes.gap: Cai et al. treat independent Gaussian noise and Bernoulli observation.  Mehrotra et al. prove an armwise matrix-row upper bound whose fourth-power logarithmic factor, structural assumptions, and loss differ; only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\) is shared.  The present converse embeds a bounded causal score with observed propensities inside the predictable class.
statement_notes.consumer: Trial designers obtain a lower benchmark linking decision budget, outcome scale, and singular signal strength.

statement_notes.justification: The first-moment form places recorded IPW--SVD in the same expected-loss criterion as the converse and the hybrid bracket.

statement_notes.justification: Nonemptiness and bounded outcomes impose a signal ceiling that reveals the true floor of every displayed uniform resolution.
statement_notes.gap: With fixed complexity and bounded aspect ratio, \(b_{nm}\) can shrink no faster than \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\), while \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\); the current uniform stochastic bounds therefore do not shrink.
statement_notes.consumer: Minimax and blind-diagnostic conclusions are interpreted only at resolutions compatible with the bounded-outcome class.

statement_notes.justification: The live question is the estimator-independent rate between \(b_{nm}\) and a constant; a sharp normalized constant is downstream of that rate decision.
